title: Find the N-th Value After K Seconds
statement:
Picture an array `a` holding `n` ones. Once per second, every entry is replaced at the same moment by the total of the old values from `a[0]` up to and including itself: `a[0]` therefore stays `1`, and the new `a[1]` is the old `a[0] + a[1]`.

Given `n` and `k`, return the last entry, `a[n - 1]`, after `k` seconds. It grows very large, so return it modulo `10^9 + 7`.
notes:
## Intuition

One second replaces the array with its own prefix sums. So the problem is simply "take prefix sums `k` times and read the last entry". Rebuilding each new value by adding up everything before it would cost O(n²) per second, but a prefix sum can be built in one left-to-right pass: the new `a[i]` is the new `a[i - 1]` plus the old `a[i]`. Doing that in place gives O(n·k), about a million additions at the limits.

(The values come from Pascal's triangle: after `s` seconds, `a[i]` is the binomial coefficient C(i + s, s), so the answer also equals C(n - 1 + k, k). The prefix-sum loop gets there without factorials or modular inverses.)

## Approach

1. Fill an array `a` of length `n` with `1`.
2. Repeat for each `second` from `1` to `k`.
3. Scan `i` from `1` to `n - 1` and set `a[i] = (a[i] + a[i - 1]) % MOD`. Because `a[i - 1]` was already updated in this pass, it holds the new prefix sum up to `i - 1`.
4. Return `a[n - 1]`.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 4`, `k = 5`, starting from `[1, 1, 1, 1]`:

| second | a |
|---|---|
| 1 | `[1, 2, 3, 4]` |
| 2 | `[1, 3, 6, 10]` |
| 3 | `[1, 4, 10, 20]` |
| 4 | `[1, 5, 15, 35]` |
| 5 | `[1, 6, 21, 56]` |

The last entry is `56`, which is also C(8, 5).

## Complexity

- Time: O(n·k): one pass of `n - 1` additions per second.
- Space: O(n) for the array, updated in place.

## Pitfalls

- Take the modulo on every addition; the true values grow like binomial coefficients and overflow quickly.
- Update in place from left to right. Going right to left would add the old `a[i - 1]` and give only a two-term sum.
- `a[0]` never changes, so the inner loop starts at `i = 1`; with `n = 1` the answer is always `1`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `MOD` | the modulus `10^9 + 7` |
| `a` | the array after the seconds processed so far |
| `second` | which second is being simulated |
| `i` | position being turned into a prefix sum |

narration.4: Simulate the k seconds one at a time.
narration.5: Rebuild the prefix sums left to right; a[0] never changes.
narration.6: a[i - 1] already holds the new prefix sum, so adding the old a[i] extends it by one position.
narration.9: After k rounds the last entry is the answer.
